question: __________ in Bihar was the capital of Magadha for several years. Later the capital was shifted to Pataliputra (present-day Patna).
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajagriha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magadha **was a great kingdom, and **its capital **for many years** was Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir) in Bihar**.
 
• It was then **renamed Pataliputra (present-day Patna).**
 
• **Udayin established Pataliputra **near the confluence of two rivers, the Son and the Ganges.
 
• He relocated his capital from** Rajgriha to Patliputra **because of the latter's** strategic location inside the empire **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mathura__ is well-known as the birthplace of Lord Krishna**, an ancient Hindu deity who is said to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. Krishna is a venerated divinity in the Hindu religion system, and Hindus see him as a true warrior and hero.
 
• **__Kalinga__ **is a historical Indian region. It is located between **the Mahanadi and the Godavari rivers.**
